speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, upon the IP right holders' request, that is, right holder-initiated actions, for imports only.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Second, by ex officio action, that is, Customs acting on their own volition, for imports, exports and goods in transit with local consignees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As such, amendments are required for our Copyright Act, Trade Marks Act, Registered Designs Act and Geographical Indications Act, collectively known in this speech as the "various IP Acts".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The border enforcement measures for geographical indications have already been introduced in the new Geographical Indications Act (GI Act), that was passed in April 2014 but not yet brought into force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This Bill now seeks to amend the Copyright Act, Trade Marks Act and the Registered Designs Act to implement our EUSFTA obligations as follows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Next, the Bill will provide new powers for Customs to obtain and provide information relating to the goods they seized or detained to facilitate the taking of infringement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, this Bill will standardise and clarify the terms and provisions relating to border enforcement across the various IP Acts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will now take the House through the main features of this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, the Bill will implement our EUSFTA obligations to enhance existing border enforcement measures in the Copyright Act and Trade Marks Act and establish a border enforcement regime in the Registered Designs Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Currently, a right-holder-initiated action under the Copyright Act and Trade Marks Act is limited to only suspected infringing goods which are to be imported into Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: No such equivalent power is found in the Registered Designs Act currently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These measures are set out in Part 1, Division 2; Part 3; and Part 4, Division 2 of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: An owner of a valid copyright or registered trade mark in Singapore, or a licensee with the power to give a notice of seizure, will be able to avail themselves of these new measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The same applies to an owner or an exclusive licensee of a registered design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Similar safeguards under the existing border enforcement regime will also apply to ensure that these new measures are not abused.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, right holders must provide a security deposit if they would like Customs to seize certain suspected infringing goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Also, a person aggrieved by the seizure can apply to the Court for compensation, if the right holder fails to take infringement action after filing a request for seizure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The second set of new features are powers for Customs to detain and provide rights holders with information relating to the infringing goods seized or detained by Customs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These powers will be provided for in the various IP Acts, and are set out in clauses 4, 7, 25, 39, 47, 53, 57, 60 and 78 of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They are intended to complement Customs’ border enforcement duty and facilitate right holders in instituting IP infringement proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The information to be provided will be limited to the names and contact details of any person connected with the import or export of the seized or detained goods that are necessary for instituting IP infringement proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In order to guard against right holders abusing this power to “fish” for information, the information sought will only be provided after Customs have seized the infringing goods, and the IP rights holders have provided Customs with a security deposit and supporting documents evidencing their IP rights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The third feature of the Bill involves standardising and clarifying the terms and provisions relating to border enforcement across the various IP Acts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, clauses 25, 47 and 78 of the Bill will clarify the processes for ex officio seizures in the Copyright Act, the Geographical Indications Act and the Trade Marks Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These changes will streamline Customs' border enforcement operations and procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Sufficient notice will be provided before the commencement of the relevant provisions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The four statutory IP rights regimes, which this Bill seeks to amend, relate to copyright, registered design, geographical indicators, and trade marks.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At this point, I should declare that I am a practising lawyer whose practice includes IP Law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: IP rights allow branding and quality assurance through exclusive access to goodwill of products from a particular brand or a place of origin.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They also allow “creators” to support themselves through their creations by recognising and protecting the property within their creations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, the Copyright (Gramophone Records and Government Broadcasting) Act 1968 was enacted to “deal with the increase in the importation and sale of pirated records of copyrighted musical works”, which “threatened the livelihood of local artistes, composers and musicians”.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, protecting IP rights prevents theft – not of tangible goods per se, but of an intangible good.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The protection of IP provides an incentive for and rewards creativity and innovation, extending even to software creation!

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By promoting innovation and art, society benefits through the protection of IP rights.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How this Bill strengthens the enforcement of IP rights is through the framework of detention, further supported by easier access to information.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, the consequences of a wrongful detention of allegedly infringed goods can be very costly and disruptive to the importer and exporter.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While the test is not new, for example, section 140IA of the current Copyright Act, I would like to ask how effective has this test been in striking the balance between swift and effective action and deterring potential misuse of power.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I would also like to seek more clarity on the difference between what the Director-General can prescribe and what the Minister can make rules on.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is in relation to the notice to request for detention of suspected infringing goods.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Director-General is to determine the form of the notice, which is supported by such documents and information as the Director-General may require, yet the Minister is to make rules for the manner in which notices are to be given and for the giving of information and evidence to the Director-General.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Additionally, the explanatory statement says that clause 35 enables forms of notices “to be determined by the Director-General (instead of being prescribed in the rules).” Because of the distinction drawn by the High Court in the case of Cheong Seok Leng, between actions that have a legislative effect and those that are executive or administrative, rule prescription and executive decisions do not seem interchangeable.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, I would like to seek clarification from the good Senior Minister of State the respective roles of the Minister and Director-General in this area.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This power to detain is supported by making it easier for the authorities and the IP right holder to get certain information.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As the phrase “any information or document that the officer considers relevant for”… “statistical or research purposes” is quite broad, I would like to seek, therefore, clarification on what sort of document, information, research or statistic is envisioned behind the grounds to get such information.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This broad access to information is augmented by preserving the privilege against self-incrimination.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am referring to the new section 140EA(5) of the Copyright Act as inserted by clause 4 and other similar clauses.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One, would a bare assertion that the information would expose a person to criminal liability be sufficient to trigger this provision; and two, the provision says that the document or information is not admissible in evidence against the person in criminal proceedings except under some circumstances, for example, where false information was provided.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But, for example, in a normal criminal trial, if the accused chooses to give evidence, he would generally need to answer any question or risk having an adverse inference drawn against him.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: According to the press release, this is “in accordance with Singapore’s EUSFTA obligations and Customs’ operational needs.” Therefore, I would like to ask, what is being done to ensure that we have sufficient operational resources such that the relevant officers will have the necessary knowledge or expertise to be able to discern what information is necessary “to enable any action to be taken in relation to future shipments of goods” and whether information sought is, indeed, “necessary” to institute infringement action?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill also seeks to rationalise border enforcement procedure across the four statutory regimes under the Copyright Act, Trade Marks Act, Registered Designs Act, and Geographical Indicators Act 2014.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: A report made in September 2017 by the International Property Rights Index, which ranks countries according to their protection of physical and IP rights, has placed Singapore as the best in the region for protection of IP rights.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: An article reported by Forbes last year, stated that numerous global studies revealed that countries with the strongest IP protections have the tendency to employ more full-time researchers, leading to greater investments in research and development (R&D) and Foreign Direct Investment.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This results in large portions of their workforce in higher paying IP-intensive organisations and industries.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: With no natural resources, and human capital as its only offering, it is by no chance that Singapore will have to emerge as a champion of IP rights, competing with other developed economies.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: While I support the Bill, I would like to highlight the following concerns with regard to the Enhanced Border Enforcement Measures under EUSFTA.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Now, my questions: how does one qualify a suspected infringing goods as genuine?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: What would happen if suspected infringing goods are proven to be not correct?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: For the enforcement under these clauses, when can we expect that these are to be implemented and enforced?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Similar to the above, the seizure of suspected infringing goods that are imported or to be exported under the Registered Design Act, when is this expected to be implemented and enforced?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Will it be on a different timeline and schedule?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Or will it be done at the same time as the above?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Moving ahead, this Bill is also intended to allow Customs to provide IPR holders with names and contact details of any persons connected with the import or export of the seized goods in facilitating IPR infringement proceedings.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: These are stipulated in clause 4 of new sub-section inserts 140EA, 140EB, 140LD and 140LE of the Copyright Act.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: While I can see the rationale and merits to these changes, thus speeding up and facilitating fast and efficient IPR infringement proceedings, nevertheless, I have the following queries: (a) why was this not implemented before?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Was there a specific reason that this has to be changed and implemented now?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: (c) Is this in any way related to EUSFTA?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: (d) Even if the information can be provided to the IPR holder after the seizure of infringed goods and security deposit has been placed and supporting documents are submitted, how do we ensure that such information is well-protected and does not fall into the wrong recipient?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: (e) Lastly, if there is a lapse in (d), is there any clause that states the course of action?

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Protection of IP rights must be taken with utmost importance and its infringement must be severely and appropriately dealt with.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The IP (Border Enforcement) Bill is a step forward in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I truly believe that not only will it re-enforce our position as a champion of IP rights; it will also bring us as one of the many international IP hubs.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, notwithstanding the comments and suggestions made, I support the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Being a country at the crossroads of the world, between east and west, north and south, as well as one of the busiest travel hubs, we must certainly put in the effort to prevent and reduce breaches in IP and our Border Enforcements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Officers and staff have to be highly vigilant, observant and astute, knowing the high numbers they have to deal with.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is critical for our Customs officers to work together with IP rights holders to protect their IPs, to conduct product training session and how to differentiate between genuine and counterfeit products.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: These differences can be so subtle, so easily missed if not handled with a high index of suspicion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How often and how extensive are the training provided for our officers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The range of products is tremendous and ever increasing, thus the need for extremely robust and updated training and knowledge.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How do our officers assess goods and products that are in transit?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there certain guidelines to ensure these are not missed or overlooked?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there border measures in Singapore for parallel imported goods?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Once the goods and products that are counterfeit are confiscated, are they all destroyed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Will there be a conduct of a fact-finding mission or an evidence-based assessment?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are our laws and policy in this aspect well aligned with other jurisdictions for some degree of uniformity?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These provisions allow information and documents possessed by the Government to be shared, upon request, for private purposes, such as research, or to institute infringement proceedings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, will the period which the information or document be retained be limited to the purpose for which it has been requested?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As for amendments allowing officers the power to require a person to provide information or documents for a statistical or research purpose, can the Senior Minister of State clarify whose statistical or research purposes these provisions refer to?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What safeguards are there to ensure that the information and documents will be kept confidential during the research process?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, amendments to the four IP Acts provide officers powers to require a person to provide information or documents to fulfil future requests for the information to institute infringement actions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How would the officer determine what information or documents might be required for the hypothetical proceedings?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would this lead to indiscriminate seizure of information or documents?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, how long would these information or documents be retained for?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the retention period be subject to the limitation period of potential claims?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When the information or documents are obtained, would the person be informed of the possibility that their information would be provided to the copyright holder for the purposes of instituting private proceedings?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I understand that the amendments also allow the Director-General to provide a person information for instituting an infringement action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The language of the provision which allows the provision of information relating to “any person connected” with the import or export of the seized goods is very broad.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the categories of connected persons intended to be covered by this provision?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is there a limit again to the period that a person may request for the information to institute an infringement action?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the person whose information is being provided be informed of the fact that the information has been shared?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, the Copyright and Trade Mark Acts simply states that the Director-General will specify a retention period for the goods, after which, it will be returned to the owner unless the objector files an infringement suit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify the retention period for alleged infringing goods if an infringement suit is started?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will they only be released after the decision of the infringement suit is out?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the meantime, what remedy does the importer or exporter have?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even if the goods are released to the original owner, pending the decision of the infringement suit, does this confer an automatic injunction on the original owner to sell the goods within Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If yes, does this injunction extend to being prohibited from further exporting the returned goods to another country and selling them there?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This could cause potential losses to the importer or exporter that may not be sufficiently remedied through the provision of security or damages.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They can issue an “Indication” which operates as a non-binding preliminary opinion on the matter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This can inform the objector or IPR holder and the alleged infringer on how they should choose to resolve the matter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Has the Ministry looked into setting up a similar review process?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also have a number of clarifications to make on the implementation of Singapore's EUSFTA obligations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These were similarly highlighted to me by IPSA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, Article 10.50 of EUSFTA requires customs authorities to adopt a range of approaches to “facilitate the effective enforcement of IP rights”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that one of the purposes of the Bill is to “standardise the terms and provisions relating to border enforcement across the IP Acts”, why are patents not afforded the same enforcement processes as copyrights, geographical indications, trademarks and registered designs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, can the Minister clarify why ex officio actions are not provided for the imports and exports of registered designs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, there is a minor inconsistency between the definition of “counterfeit trademark goods” under EUSFTA and the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the EUSFTA Article 10.48(b), it is defined as goods bearing a trademark that is identical or “which cannot be distinguished in its essential aspects”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In contrast, it is defined under section 3(5) and (6) of the Trade Marks Act as a good that has a sign that is identical or is so identical “as to be calculated to deceive”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This requirement of an intention to deceive is noticeably lacking from the EUSFTA’s definition, which, therefore, appears to be slightly broader than that under the Trade Marks Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I also appreciate the IPSA's inputs to Mr Louis Ng and I thank them for their contributions as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members have raised several points for clarification and I would break them down into four main areas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They are, firstly, the scope of the Bill; secondly, the border enforcement process and how it compares with other jurisdictions; and thirdly, Customs’ powers to request and provide information or documents; and finally, the timeline for implementing the Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In relation to the scope of the Bill, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Christopher de Souza enquired specifically about goods in transit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Goods in transit are, by definition, here for only a short duration of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, Customs officers will still perform the usual checks, and when they detect suspected IP infringing goods, they will convey the information to their counterparts in the destination country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, to address Mr Christopher de Souza's question, there are no similar international obligations for geographical indications and registered designs, and we, therefore, make no distinction between goods in transit with a local consignee and goods in transit without a local consignee for geographical indications and registered designs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To aid Customs, IPR holders can provide information on shipments that are suspected to contain IP infringing goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked why the Bill does not implement border enforcement measures for patents and ex officio action for registered designs, as part of our obligations under Article 10.50 of EUSFTA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, it is also impracticable to do so because the detection of a suspected patent infringing good generally requires a higher level of specialised technical knowledge and expertise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Patents are, therefore, unlike copyright, trade marks, registered designs and geographical indications, where a visual inspection can usually be used to detect the IP infringement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Given the high level of specialisation required to detect patent infringing goods, it is not feasible for Customs officers to make such assessments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are also no international obligations to take ex officio action in relation to registered designs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Unlike copyright or trade marks, it is difficult for our Customs officers to identify whether particular goods infringe a registered design without any information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, where a registered design owner files a formal request for seizure with specific information to identify a shipment with goods suspected of infringing registered designs, for example, when the shipment will reach Singapore, our Customs officers can assist in detecting and seizing such goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I hope that addresses Mr Louis Ng’s queries.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Louis Ng also sought clarification on the rationale for the difference between the terminology and definition of "counterfeit trademark goods" between the EUSFTA definitions and section 3(5) and 3(6) of the Trade Marks Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The definitions in both provisions are substantially similar and Mr Louis Ng may also know that the definition was put into force in the Trade Marks Act in 2004, which is about 14 to 15 years ago, and we have kept that definition throughout.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the intention is to remain with that definition, but the level of obligation would not deviate substantially or materially from the EUSFTA definition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah asked whether our border enforcement regime covers parallel imports and goods in travellers' personal luggage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Parallel imports are not counterfeit goods and are, therefore, not considered infringing under our IP laws.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This has been the case even before these amendments apply.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will now turn to questions on our border enforcement processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By definition, in enhancing the border enforcement provisions through this Bill, it necessarily comes with enhanced powers and with some additional degree of intervention.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With that, Members have raised several queries on the processes involved where goods are seized, for example, the period of detention, whether they will be destroyed, how a defendant can show that the goods are genuine, and the remedies available where the goods were wrongly detained and found to be non-infringing.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think the majority of the Members raised questions around these few issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The various IP Acts all contain a framework to ensure that there is due process in the manner in which seized goods are dealt with, and I will now briefly describe this framework.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Upon seizure, Customs will notify IPR holders to verify the authenticity of the goods and commence civil actions for IP infringement against relevant parties within the period specified in Customs’ notice, or any extended period, as may be so notified.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The status of the goods will then depend on whether an infringement action is commenced.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where an infringement action is commenced, the importer or exporter will be notified by the IPR holder if he is the defendant to the action and have the opportunity to defend himself in Court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, to address Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef's query, the Court process will entail fact-finding and an evidence-based assessment, in relation to the relevant copyright and IP provisions that are currently in place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whether such a Court order is granted or not, will be decided by the Court on a case-by-case basis, applying again, the relevant IP provisions and laws.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where there is no such Court order, the goods shall be released.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whether an individual is liable for IP infringement or not will be determined by the Courts based on the facts of a particular case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The goods will then be returned to the importer or exporter as the case may be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In a situation where no infringement action is taken, any person aggrieved by the seizure may then apply to the Court for an order of compensation for any loss or damage suffered as a result of the seizure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza raised a question on that, and quite rightly so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The legal regime does protect the person in such a situation where no subsequent follow-up infringement action is then taken by the right holder.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Court may order compensation in such amount as the Court thinks fit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The goods will then be released to the importer or exporter.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked: "how effective   has been in striking the balance between swift and effective action in deterring potential misuse of power”.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I now move on to the proposed expedited review process or indication that Mr Louis Ng and, through the help of IPSA, has raised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The proposal is a thoughtful one, and one that we can consider further.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But so far, the evidence we have suggests that IPR holders are already capable themselves of making a quick assessment on whether there are goods which have infringed their IP rights or not.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, it will be in their interest to do so, because if someone is peddling infringing goods, then it will be in the right holder's interest to move quickly and act swiftly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where an expedited decision is required, parties can seek a summary judgment from the Court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is also a procedure they can avail themselves of, setting out their grounds.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nonetheless, we welcome IPSA to provide us with more details, as I said earlier about this proposal, which we can then consider further.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will now turn to deal with Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef's question on the training that is provided for our Customs officers to identify counterfeit goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Presently, Customs has already worked with a number of brand owners to conduct training for officers from Customs, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) and the Singapore Police Force IP Rights Branch to look at, evaluate and discern between genuine and counterfeit goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not always easy, but it is something that we work very closely with the brand owners.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Upon detecting suspected counterfeit goods, our officers will also engage the IPR holders to seek verification of the authenticity of the goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza sought clarification on the difference between what the Director-General of Customs can prescribe and what the Minister can make rules on, particularly in relation to the notice to request for detention of suspected infringing goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The clauses 12, 25, 35, 47, 53, 65 and 78 of the Bill grant the Minister the power to make the necessary rules and regulations to provide for, amongst others, the manner in which notices have been given, and for the giving of information and evidence, where the rules and regulations have a legislative effect.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I know that Mr Christopher de Souza drew our attention to the case in question but, in this case, the Customs Director-General is given the discretion to determine the specific form of notice – in other words, what exactly is the form he needs, what are the documents or information that is required in that particular case – having had the powers already prescribed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are administrative in nature and, therefore, need not be legislated by the Minister, as the case is generally for forms that are administered by public agencies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are forms which will be readily accessible to the public on the website of Customs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I turn now to address Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef's query on whether our border enforcement laws and policy align with those of other jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The short answer is, generally yes, although inevitable differences will exist from one country to another, depending on the local context and flavour.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These measures allow IPR holders to request Customs officers to seize suspected copyright and trade mark infringing goods that are imported into the country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many other established jurisdictions, such as the US, the EU and Australia also provide further border protection mechanisms which extend to ex officio action and other types of IP infringements.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of these jurisdictions also cover goods which are to be exported as well, as we are now seeking to do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Customs has been and will continue to handle sensitive commercial data obtained from traders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They are empowered to disclose such information as necessary to IPR holders or use such information internally for border enforcement purpose.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These powers are given to Customs so as to facilitate the administration of justice and uphold our reputation of having a strong IP enforcement regime.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nonetheless, let me reassure traders at the outset that confidentiality of their data will be respected.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Their data will remain confidential and will be used or provided only under limited circumstances in relation to the border enforcement matters as legislated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I wish to now address the Members' queries on this matter in some greater detail: first, on the rationale for introducing these powers; and second, Customs' power to request information; and finally, Customs' power to provide the information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the course of Customs’ border enforcement work over the years, this was one area that was identified that needed some streamlining and which they felt would facilitate the work that it had, with these adjunct and peripheral powers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The need to amend our legislation to fulfil our EUSFTA obligations now gives us the opportunity to do so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I would also add that the EUSFTA, whilst concluded in 2014, was a subject of some challenge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was only in the course of last year, 2017, that the EU Court of Justice pronounced that the EU entering into it was competent to do so and was able to proceed with it, and hence, we waited till this time to introduce our Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Various Members have asked about the scope of Customs' power to request information, the relevant safeguards, and the privilege against self-incrimination in relation to the requested information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will regard that as quite basic information before such actions can be instituted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, to facilitate enforcement against future shipments of goods; and third, for other statistical or research purposes relating to border enforcement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Various Members have raised this point about information being requested.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It would more likely than not in most cases include commercial invoices, packing lists, bill of lading, airwaybill or shippers’ details and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, information that will allow one to identify the goods, identify the source and the shipper and perhaps its destination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are all useful for identifying the relevant parties involved in suspected IP infringement and the activities around the IP infringement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As for the type of information that can be requested for “statistical or research purposes”, this refers to information that can help Customs build profiles of high-risk shipments and also enhance their capabilities to anticipate and target shipments which tend to be involved in shipping IP infringing goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These will be details, such as the names and contact details of the importer or exporter, and the description of goods and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, to add to the Customs database, to ensure that, in future, these mechanisms become more and more sophisticated and Customs can be better equipped to anticipate and also target these specific shipments in question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Christopher de Souza also asked what is being done to ensure that Customs are able to determine or discern the necessary information that should be requested for the three stated purposes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Customs will conduct relevant training for their officers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is also a new area in terms of the enforcement and so training will be done for the officers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They will seek to put in place a standard operating procedure as far as possible to make the guidance available to Customs officers to guide them in terms of seeking the relevant type of information and to be more discerning and to be able to raise the right questions and focus their minds on the right issues and the right observations in relation to the three stated purposes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked whether there is a limited period that Customs will retain the information for, and what this period will be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Customs will retain the information to the extent the purpose for collecting the information remains relevant and also, generally, in accordance with the Government’s record-retention policy, depending on the platform on which the information is received.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Next, I will address the concerns raised by Mr Louis Ng and Mr Azmoon Ahmad on the safeguards relating to the information requested by Customs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, a person will be informed about the purpose for Customs’ request for his information at the point of request, and not when the information is shared with an IPR holder for the purposes of instituting infringement actions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, there are safeguards to ensure that the information will be kept confidential, particularly during the research process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The information must be used strictly and only for the three purposes, as explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Each request for the information and each proposed use of the information by Customs officers for research or statistical purposes will be considered carefully.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, the information disclosed to the domestic public agencies will also be governed by the Official Secrets Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza raised two questions regarding the privilege against self-incrimination that is provided in connection with the obligation to provide information as requested by Customs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, he asked whether a bare assertion that the information would expose a person to criminal liability will be sufficient to trigger the privilege.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This would, of course, also be something which the Court takes into account as may be appropriate as it would do with any proposed adverse influences to be drawn, as Mr Christopher de Souza raised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, he also sought clarification on the extent to which the privilege against self-incrimination is meant to operate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The statement cannot be used at trial, whether as corroboration or for impeachment, as Mr Christopher de Souza knows.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the Prosecution's case then has to be based on other evidence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, where a person provides false information, that is quite a different situation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Such information may then be admissible against him in a prosecution for an offence for providing false information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It will not be justifiable to shield or protect a person from being prosecuted for providing false information as this will be entirely contrary to the interests of justice.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Next, I will clarify the points that Mr Louis Ng raised about the scope of Customs’ power to provide information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first relates to the categories of persons whose names and contact details may be disclosed to IPR holders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are persons, whom I think I referred to earlier, who are likely to be the importer, exporter, consignee or any other person involved in the shipping chain from which the IP infringing goods were seized.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second point that Mr Louis Ng raised concerns the timeframe within which a person may request for information to institute an infringement action.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is no specific timeframe in the Act itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, for reasons that I have outlined earlier, it will be in the interest of the right holder to move expeditiously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is also because there is a stipulated timeline within which he must institute infringement action in relation to the seized goods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, I think it would be expedient to seek the information within this timeline, and not outside.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this context, he has also got to do so after providing Customs with a security deposit and supporting documents evidencing their IP rights.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The enhanced border enforcement measures for copyright and trade marks will be effected once the EUSFTA enters into force or comes into force.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As explained earlier, it has not yet come into force.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we will have the measures coincide with that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have explained at the outset, it gives time for businesses and people to adjust to it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I mentioned earlier, sufficient notice will also be provided before the commencement of the relevant provisions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Bill represents our commitment to honour our international obligations by strengthening our border enforcement processes and also instill in us the importance of upholding IP rights, as Mr Christopher de Souza mentioned.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is critical not only to IP but also to various aspects of business in Singapore.
